# Vejle: Børne- Og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium

Vejle: Børne- Og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium (also referred to in reports as PSY Børne- Og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium (Vejle)) is a child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinic operating within [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src4]. The clinic is evaluated annually through the Danish ADHD-DATABASEN, which tracks adherence to national diagnostic standards and clinical guidelines across different age groups and geographic regions.

The clinic is particularly notable for its exceptional performance regarding [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]], a quality metric that measures the proportion of ADHD assessment pathways for children aged 0–5 where a clinical environmental observation is conducted within 120 days of the assessment's start. In the 2023/24 reporting period, Vejle achieved a 100% target fulfillment rate (14 out of 14 cases) for this indicator [^src1]. It was one of only two departments in the country, alongside [[aabenna-borne-og-ungdomspsykiatrisk-ambulatorium|Aabenraa: Børne og Ungdomspsykiatrisk Ambulatorium]], to reach the development goal for Indikator 2a with a perfect 100% fulfillment rate [^src2]. This consistent success highlights the clinic's strong adherence to diagnostic protocols for very young children.

However, the clinic's performance varies significantly when evaluating older demographics and other diagnostic metrics. For [[indicator-2b]], which tracks the use of structured diagnostic interviews or environmental observations for children aged 6–17 within 120 days, Vejle recorded a fulfillment rate of 58% (95% CI: 53–63) in 2023/24 [^src4]. While this is above the national average of 48%, it still falls short of the ≥90% standard. Furthermore, regarding [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], which measures the use of diagnostic conferences, Vejle recorded the lowest performance among departments handling more than three pathways, dropping to an 8% fulfillment rate [^src3]. 

These mixed results illustrate the broader systemic challenges documented in the national ADHD reports, where clinics may excel in specific age brackets or workflows while struggling with others due to resource constraints, varying clinical practices, or registration issues.
